newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares reach up to new record highs.
newsitem.headline: German shares reach up to new record highs.

text.p: German shares climbed to new record highs on Monday, boosted by strength in the dollar, which benefits German exporters, and gains in bourse newcomer Deutsche Telekom.
The German DAX index of 30 top shares ended floor trade at a record bourse level of 2,799.19 points, up 35.50 points, or 1.28 percent, just above an all-time high of 2,799.05 reached on November 15.
After the bourse close the DAX mounted the psychological and technical level of 2,800 points to touch a new record high in IBIS computer dealings of 2,805.75 points.
Dealers had been expecting that the 2,800 point level would be breached this week, but were surprised by the speed of the climb. They said the next target for the DAX would be 2,820 points.

Shares in telecommunications giant Telekom ended up three percent, or 96 pfennigs at 32.98 marks. Dealers said an initial wave of speculative profit-taking had come to an end, with the stock also recovering somewhat in Friday's New York trade.
The chemicals and carmaker sectors were helped by the firmer dollar, which was up nearly a pfennig on its Friday closing level, firmly above 1.51 marks.
One of the most heavily traded in the auto sector was industrial group Daimler-Benz, which ended up almost two percent, or 1.65 marks, at 99.10 marks.

There was little immediate market reaction to the latest state consumer price index reports out of Hesse, Bavaria and North Rhein-Westphalia, which showed declining or unchanged month-on-month inflation, but the figures were generally supportive for positive sentiment.

Together with figures out of Baden Wuerttemberg, the data from the states makes up preliminary west German consumer price data, likely to be reported by the Federal Statistics office later on Monday or Tuesday.
